_meta.purpose: Turkish -> English key map for the AI Supply Index series (ai-arz-serisi.ndjson).
_meta.why_keys_are_turkish: The series is append-only and OpenTimestamps-stamped. Renaming keys in place would make earlier lines unreadable and put two schemas in one file. The keys are therefore FROZEN; this map is the English contract, and to_english.py generates an English-keyed mirror (series-en.ndjson) without touching the original.
_meta.source_of_truth: This file. The Schema table in README.md is generated from it via `python3 to_english.py --schema-md`.

histogram_buckets.rule: Every direct child of a `histogram` object is a numeric bucket label produced at runtime (e.g. "<1", "1-10", ">=10000"). These are DATA, not schema, and are copied through unchanged.

package_identifiers.rule: For the endpoints listed below, every direct child of `ozet` is a package or repository identifier chosen at runtime. These are DATA, not schema, and are copied through unchanged.

groups.name: Record envelope
groups.note: Present on every line of the series. One line = one endpoint in one run.
keys: when the run started; all rows of one run share this value, so it doubles as the run id
collector version that wrote the row (absent on the very first v0.1 rows)
free-text annotation about the endpoint's limits; rows written before 2026-08-18 carry Turkish text
the measurement itself; its shape depends on the endpoint
OK | HATA (error) | HTTP-HATA (http error) | HATA-ICERIDE (error inside the summary)
HTTP status code, only present when the request failed
Python exception repr, truncated; only present on failure
endpoint URL (v0.1 rows only; later versions record it in `not`)
raw response size (v0.1 rows only); raw payloads are not stored

groups.name: Distribution summary
groups.note: Emitted by the shared `dagilim_ozeti` helper and reused wherever a distribution is archived (x402, Sherlock, Apify, Hugging Face, DeFiLlama). The distribution is the point: totals alone hide concentration.
keys: how many numeric values entered the distribution
how many of the values were exactly 0
bucket label -> count; bucket labels are data (see passthrough)
share of the total held by the single largest value — the concentration measure
share of the total held by the ten largest values

groups.name: Pagination and coverage
groups.note: Shared across the paginated endpoints. These exist so a reader can tell a real zero from an unmeasured one.
keys: how many pages the collector actually fetched
how many items were collected across those pages
page count the API itself reported (Sherlock)
how many items yielded a usable numeric value
explicit statement of what this sample is and is not (e.g. upper tier, not a median)

PRESENT ONLY WHEN THE SCHEMA BROKE. If this key exists, the accompanying value is NOT zero — it is UNKNOWN. The collector refuses to silently count 0 when a response changes shape; it records why instead. Treat a row carrying `unmeasurable` as missing data, never as a measured zero.

groups.name: Open-window watch
groups.note: Endpoints sherlock_contests, code4rena_audits (and cantina_competitions, implemented but not yet wired). Answers 'how many doors are open right now', which is a different question from 'how many exist'.
keys: total competitions/audits the platform lists; null when unmeasurable
how many are open right now (end time in the future); null when unmeasurable
of those, how many are open to the public (not private/invite-only)
the open ones themselves, soonest deadline first, capped at 10 per row to bound record size; the counts above are always exact
which platform the entry came from: sherlock | code4rena | cantina
platform's own identifier for the entry
true when the entry is open to anyone rather than invite-only
days remaining at the moment of measurement
prize pool as the platform reports it (format varies by platform)
platform's own category label, e.g. contest type or audit type
whether the platform requires identity verification (Cantina only)

groups.name: x402 discovery
groups.note: Agent-payment resource registry. ROLLING 30-DAY WINDOW: the upstream keeps no history, so a week not captured is gone.
keys: resources registered in the discovery index
distribution of paid calls per resource over the last 30 days
distribution of unique payers per resource over the last 30 days
call count for one resource (inside top10_by_calls)

groups.name: Sherlock leaderboard
groups.note: Cumulative lifetime payouts per security researcher. There is no date parameter upstream — this is a running total, not a period figure.
keys: how many of them have a numeric payout
distribution of lifetime earnings in USD
the ten largest entries (also used by Apify and Hugging Face)

groups.name: DeFiLlama
groups.note: Two endpoints: the AI-Agents category cross-section, and the daily revenue series of the single largest protocol in it.
keys: protocols DeFiLlama files under an AI-Agent category
protocols in the whole fees dataset, for context
summed 24h fee revenue across AI-agent protocols
how many protocols contributed a number to that sum
five largest AI-agent protocols by 30-day revenue
distribution of 30-day revenue across AI-agent protocols — where concentration becomes visible
the single protocol tracked in detail
days available in that protocol's daily series
first day present in the daily series
last day present in the daily series
distribution of the protocol's daily revenue over the last 30 days

groups.name: Apify store
groups.note: Published automation actors. SAMPLED: top 1,000 by popularity, which is an upper tier and explicitly not the store median.
keys: distribution of users per actor across the sample

groups.name: Hugging Face
groups.note: Top 100 models by download count. Downloads are cumulative and there is no official historical endpoint — this series is the archive.
keys: distribution of cumulative downloads across the sample

groups.name: npm downloads
groups.note: Per-package download volume. The upstream clips the range to roughly 547 days, so old data falls off and must be archived.
keys: first day of the returned range
last day of the returned range
downloads summed over the returned 30-day range
the final day's raw record, kept as a spot check
downloads on that day (upstream key, already English)
the day itself (upstream key, already English)

groups.name: PyPI downloads
groups.note: Per-package download volume excluding mirror traffic. The upstream window is roughly 362 days, so old data falls off.
keys: earliest date in the returned window
latest date in the returned window
total non-mirror downloads across the window
non-mirror downloads over the last 30 days of the window

groups.name: GitHub repositories
groups.note: Point-in-time snapshot of agent-framework repositories. GitHub exposes no historical star series here, so each run is one archived point.
keys: open issues (GitHub counts pull requests here too)
most recent push to the default branch
